application_review: All 490 baseline source/config hashes were revalidated before registration of six new modules. Only Hindman168.lean imports and Verification.lean exact-name reports changed among retained files. All prior proof modules, StrongStatement, nine PNT+ source modules and Lean/mathlib/PNT+ pins are unchanged. The fixed local correlation and prediction sections still match adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a after newline normalization. No official or remote update was checked in this goal round.

The prime divisor multiplier is p*1_{p|z} on all integers. Its expectation is exactly the total of the original unnormalized integerEtaMass, and its squared expectation is p times that total. Signed or negative integer arguments are covered by the existing original harmonic transport.

The actual harmonic prime weights satisfy sum_p lambda(p)^2*p=1/S. The weighted diagonal mass is exactly sum_p lambda(p)^2*p*total(integerEtaMass_p), with both independent fresh sampling atoms retained. This is the p^2*P(p|Y) diagonal in the paper, not an unweighted collision estimate.

Uniform residue-error monotonicity bounds the weighted diagonal by (1+residueError_K)/S. The nonnegative recorded cap uses (1+abs(residueError_K))/S. Its inverse-power rate follows from actual master pool harmonic-mass growth and actual earlier-pool upper-endpoint sampling growth; no pool-upper monotonicity or vanishing-error premise is added.

Actual pool primes are eventually primorial units by lower-endpoint growth beyond the earlier auxiliary budget and the derived primorial<=modulus<=auxiliary bound. Gap divisibility, rather than any pool monotonicity, supplies later-pivot logarithmic growth. The finite varying-index choice is over the fixed master index set.

Each intermediate outer law keeps its original old-prime tuple and original independent harmonic coordinates. The fresh-prime diagonal majorant at any selected column marginalizes exactly to the actual one-coordinate harmonic weighted diagonal mass. The other coordinates and the old-prime tuple are marginalized using their derived total-one laws, without conditioning on an unrelated good event.

For arbitrary supported integrands bounded by V^B*eta_p*eta_q, the full-minus-off-diagonal average is controlled by V^B times the actual diagonal cap. The cap tends to zero after any fixed polynomial loss. Uniformity over the test functions is explicit in the eventual inequality and its epsilon form; the old-prime tuple is shared.

The intermediate row divisor masks lie in [0,V] at the actual earlier-gap auxiliary budget, since the chain tails lie before that gap. This uses the exact actual tail-divisor probability and support laws. It does not use the incompatible larger pivot auxiliary budget as the smaller cap.

The actual invariant-row density is bounded by V^(2*maskRowCountBound m), using 1+V<=V^2 for V>=2 and the actual row-count bound. The doubled integrand Omega*g_p*g_q is therefore bounded by V^(2*maskRowCountBound m+2*B)*eta_p*eta_q when each g has the stated supported eta-weighted cap.

The previous actual weighted-square inequality is combined with diagonal deletion without changing its m-only coefficient 2^(maskRowCountBound m)+1. The explicit loss is that coefficient times V^(2*K+2*B) times the diagonal cap, and is proved to tend to zero. The off-diagonal average remains signed; no unjustified nonnegativity assumption is used.

Distinct supported primes are coprime. Integer divisibility is transported through natAbs, proving eta_p*eta_q=eta_{p*q} on all integers. The comparison expectation is identified exactly with the original unnormalized integerEtaMass at p*q.

The actual harmonic law dilated by p*q is compared to that unnormalized divisor law with a uniform endpoint-squared dilation cap. Its inverse-power rate follows from the existing earlier-pool polynomial affine log-growth theorem at degree two. Fixed polynomial sup losses are absorbed, and the resulting uniform bound covers every pair of distinct actual pool primes and every bounded test.

The pq transfer is currently a single-coordinate theorem. It has not yet been composed with the full old-prime/remaining-coordinate sampling law or identified with the two concrete descendant integrands with branch multipliers (q,p) and (p,q). The weighted-square theorem likewise assumes a supported eta-weighted polynomial bound on g; prime insertion and actual descendant-function construction remain to be proved.
